title: SLO Change Experiment Lab and Rollback Playbook
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook lays out a repeatable, low-risk way to run controlled SLO change experiments (adjustments to targets, weighting, or counting rules) on Redwood Inference services. It covers experiment design, telemetry and gating, phased traffic rollout, capacity hedging, automated rollback triggers, and acceptance criteria once the experiment ends. The aim is to get high-confidence evidence of customer-visible impact before an SLO change is adopted company-wide.

Scope
-----
Applies to: inference-gateway, realtime-api, batcher, embed-service, and colocated model-serving nodes.
Out of scope: platform billing SLOs and external partner SLAs, which go through the contracts team process.

When to use this lab
--------------------
- Changing a latency SLO (e.g., P95 target from 150ms -> 120ms)
- Changing how error budget is counted (e.g., moving from 4xx+5xx to 5xx-only)
- Re-weighting SLOs for multi-tenant teams
- Trying new fallback or degradation behaviors that affect SLOs

Prerequisites
-------------
1) Service owners named and on-call coverage confirmed for the experiment window.
2) Synthetic canaries running for the SLO (canary-suite: inference-p95, embed-throughput).
3) Observability deck current: dashboards, SLO pulse, burn-rate alerting, latency drill-downs.
4) Capacity hedges in place (warm pools, burst absorber, pre-provisioned nodes).
5) Announcement in #sre-experiments plus an SLO-experiments-calendar entry.

Roles & ownership
------------------
- Experiment Owner: owns the plan, the run, and the postmortem. (Example: Priya Nair)
- Service Owner: handles service-level mitigations and logs. (Example: Miguel Ramos - inference-gateway)
- Observability Engineer: makes sure SLO metrics and burn rate are instrumented and actionable.
- SRE Safety Lead: can abort any experiment when a safety gate trips.

Designing the experiment
------------------------
1) State the hypothesis in one sentence. Example: "Lowering the realtime-api P95 SLO target from 150ms to 130ms will not push 5xx error-rate above 0.3% at 5% traffic under the current autoscale policy."
2) Pick primary and secondary metrics:
   - Primary: SLO burn rate over 30m windows; realtime-api P95 latency.
   - Secondary: 5xx rate, tail memory OOM count, cache miss-rate, customer-perceived error rate (sampled tokens).
3) Set pass/fail criteria:
   - Pass: cohort burn rate <= 1.0 over 2 hours and 5xx rate delta < 0.1 percentage points against baseline.
   - Fail: burn rate >= 3.0 sustained for 10 minutes or 5xx rate delta >= 0.5 percentage points.
4) Choose cohorts and durations (see Traffic Phases).

Traffic Phases (example)
------------------------
Phase | Cohort % | Duration | Objective
------|----------|----------|---------
Baseline | 0% | 30m | Record pre-change baseline metrics
Canary | 1% | 30m | Correctness smoke test at small load
Ramp1 | 5% | 1h | Check metrics and capacity hedges
Ramp2 | 15% | 2h | Look for tail effects and cross-tenant interactions
Full | 100% (optional) | 24h | Green experiments with product approval only

Telemetry & gating
------------------
- SLO burn-rate alerting has three severities
  - advisory: burn_rate >= 0.8 (informational)
  - action: burn_rate >= 1.5 for 10m (auto-scaling/traffic-hold)
  - abort: burn_rate >= 3.0 for 10m (automated rollback)
- Error-rate gate: abort when 5xx_rate_delta >= 0.5
- System health gates: OOM_count > 0 or sustained CPU_util increase > 40% -> abort
- Evidence capture: every gate logs against the experiment run id and attaches traces for the first 200 failing requests

Automated controls (operational tooling)
---------------------------------------
The experiment pipeline relies on two automation primitives:
1) Traffic controller (redwood-experiments) - sets route weights and records the cohort id.
2) Safety orchestrator (sre-safety) - listens for burn-rate alerts and rolls back when abort criteria are met.

CLI examples
------------
# Create experiment:
redwood-experiments create --service realtime-api --change '{"slo.p95_target_ms":130}' --owner priya.nair --id re-slo-exp-2026-02
# Ramp to 5%:
redwood-experiments set-weight --id re-slo-exp-2026-02 --cohort canary --weight 0.05
# Abort (manual):
redwood-experiments abort --id re-slo-exp-2026-02 --reason "observed burn-rate spike"

Runbook: Execute the SLO change experiment (step-by-step)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Pre-run checklist (T-48h):
   - Notify stakeholders and book the calendar entry.
   - Confirm the synthetic canary suite has been green for 24h.
   - Warm the capacity hedges: 5% warm pool pre-provisioned for realtime-api.
2) Open an experiment record in the experiments tracker and attach the plan.
3) Baseline capture (30m): record metrics and snapshot autoscale state.
4) Apply the config change on a single node behind a feature flag where possible (dry run).
5) Canary (1%): watch burn rate, errors, and traces. Advisory alerts should be investigated, but the run can continue.
6) Ramp1 (5%): after 30m stable, move to 5% and run two targeted load patterns (short tail-heavy and long streaming).
7) Ramp2 (15%): check cross-tenant interference and KV cache hit behavior.
8) Decision point: if pass criteria hold, proceed to product signoff; if abort criteria hit, the automated rollback runs and the incident review path applies.

Rollback procedure (automated + manual)
--------------------------------------
Automated rollback (preferred):
- Trigger: an abort gate fires (see Telemetry & gating).
- Action: the safety orchestrator calls redwood-experiments abort, restores traffic weights from the pre-experiment snapshot, and tells the autoscaler to return to baseline pools.
- Notifications: page the SRE Safety Lead, post in #sre-incidents, and open an incident record tagged with the experiment-id.

Manual rollback (if automation is unavailable):
1) Service owner runs: redwood-experiments abort --id <exp-id> --reason "manual abort"
2) Revert the config in config-store: git revert <commit> && deploy the revert with canary cadence.
3) For stateful changes (cache or schema), follow the recovery migration steps in the service runbook.

Post-experiment: acceptance criteria & postmortem
------------------------------------------------
- Acceptance checklist (complete within 24h of experiment end):
  - All cohorts back at nominal traffic weights.
  - No residual elevated error-rates over the last 72h.
  - Synthetic canaries green for 24h.
  - Observed deltas and instrumentation gaps written up.
- Postmortem (failures or unexpected impact):
  - Postmortem write-up within 3 days, with evidence links, raw traces, and the experiment run id.
  - List mitigation changes (config, autoscale thresholds, cache sizing).
  - Plan follow-up experiments if the hypothesis is inconclusive.

Capacity planning & hedging guidance
-----------------------------------
- Keep a warm pool of at least 5% of 99th percentile concurrency for the service under experiment.
- Maintain a shared burst absorber pool for model-serving sized for 2x normal short-term burst for up to 30m.
- Update the capacity playbook when an experiment shows a systematic headroom change > 15%.

Template: experiment metadata (YAML)
----------------------------------
experiment_id: re-slo-exp-2026-02
service: realtime-api
change_summary: "p95 target 150->130 ms; counting rule unchanged"
hypothesis: "No material increase in 5xx or burn rate at 5% traffic"
owner: priya.nair@redwood.ai
start_window: "2026-02-10T14:00:00Z"
phases:
  - {name: baseline, pct: 0, duration_min: 30}
  - {name: canary, pct: 1, duration_min: 30}
  - {name: ramp1, pct: 5, duration_min: 60}
  - {name: ramp2, pct: 15, duration_min: 120}
abort_criteria:
  - "burn_rate >= 3.0 for 10m"
  - "5xx_rate_delta >= 0.5"

Evidence & artifacts to collect
-------------------------------
- Experiment manifest and config snapshots (git commit ids).
- Synthetic canary traces and raw request samples for the first 200 failures.
- Autoscaler events and node provisioning timelines.
- Queryable SLO burn logs and alert history.

Acceptance decision matrix (quick)
---------------------------------
- Green: pass criteria met -> product review -> gradual rollout
- Yellow: partial signals or instrumentation gaps -> design a follow-up test -> re-run after fixes
- Red: abort criteria or other regressions -> rollback, full postmortem, capacity remediation

Related pages & references
-------------------------
- SLO observability pipeline spec: /confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/slo-observability-pipeline-design-and-validation-2025
- Runbook: SLO rollout readiness and capacity checklist

Notes & improvement backlog
--------------------------
- Bring per-tenant synthetic canaries into experiments to cut cross-tenant noise.
- Snapshot and diff autoscaler policies automatically at experiment start/stop.

Owners and contacts
